summary: 14-day Nightscout telemetry analysis reveals exceptionally strong glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), 0.3% Time Above Range (>180 mg/dL), and a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Current basal segments, carb ratios, ISF, and DIA parameters are highly accurate. Micro-excursions reaching 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches stem from meal absorption timing rather than profile parameter deficiencies.

analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 continuous 15-minute CGM readings over 14 days representing 100.0% coverage with zero data gaps >15 minutes.
analysis_steps.findings: Data completeness, sensor cadence, and treatment record linkage are optimal for profile evaluation.

analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, TAR 0.3%, TBR 0.0%, SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%. Isolated glucose dips down to 70-71 mg/dL recorded during early morning hours (02:47-03:02 UTC on Aug 11 and Aug 17).
analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic variability is remarkably low with zero clinical hypoglycemia. Overall safety profile is excellent.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unrecorded manual carb rescue logs if any occurred during early morning dips, though loop status indicates routine automated delivery.

analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight glucose averages 103.1-107.5 mg/dL (target range 95-110 mg/dL). Late afternoon inter-meal glucose remains stable at 108.3-116.7 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal segments (0.85, 0.95, 0.90, 1.05 U/h) accurately match baseline metabolic needs without driving nocturnal hypoglycemia or daylight drifts.

analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast (42g carbs, CR 10 g/U) returns to baseline by 240m (-2 mg/dL). Weekend brunch (68g carbs, CR 11 g/U) peaks at 188 mg/dL but returns to baseline by 240m (-11 mg/dL). Dinner (54g carbs, CR 9 g/U) displays predictable 120m rises (+15 to +41 mg/dL) with complete 360m recovery.
analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios, ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U), and DIA (5.5h) are accurately set. Brunch excursions represent timing/composition mismatches rather than CR errors.

analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3 min, max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min, min_5m_carbimpact=3 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM configuration settings respond safely to meal entry variations without causing over-bolusing or secondary hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific activation toggle flags (e.g., smb_always_enabled) are null in profile JSON schema.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits effectively bound automated delivery without artificially constraining loop responsiveness during postprandial rises.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens enablement flags are null in profile schema.

analysis_steps.evidence: Declared weekday breakfast strategy (20m prebolus, 70% immediate) achieves optimal postprandial control. Weekend brunch (10m prebolus, 60% immediate) exhibits transient peaks up to 188 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Advancing weekend brunch prebolus by 5-10 minutes is indicated to reduce peak 120m excursions while maintaining current split percentages.

analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch declared strategy includes 20.0g e-carbs over 120 min with a 15 min start offset.
analysis_steps.findings: E-carb modeling accurately prevents late postprandial rises from high-fat/protein meal components, matching observed 4-hour recovery.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis across all 14 days confirms that basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets, and automation limits operate harmoniously.
analysis_steps.findings: All core profile parameters should be maintained. Optimization focus is strictly placed on fine-tuning meal prebolus timing for weekend brunches.

strengths: Exceptional 99.7% Time in Range with 0.0% Time Below Range over 14 days.
Very low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%, SD 15.1 mg/dL).
Highly accurate overnight and fasting basal rate calibration.
Well-balanced CR and ISF settings across all time segments.
issues: Minor, transient postprandial glucose peaks up to 188 mg/dL during high-carb/high-fat weekend brunches.

recommendations.title: Optimize Weekend Brunch Prebolus Timing
recommendations.description: Telemetry shows glucose peaking at 180-188 mg/dL at 120 minutes post-brunch before returning smoothly to baseline by 240 minutes. Extending prebolus lead time from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes while maintaining the 60% immediate / 20g e-carb split will reduce the peak excursion without increasing hypoglycemia risk.

recommendations.description: Core SMB and Autosens delivery settings are functioning well, but specific boolean activation flags returned null in the JSON export context. Verify in AAPS preferences that 'SMB with COB' and 'Autosens' switches match intended operational preferences.

profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor postprandial response during weekend brunch after adjusting prebolus lead time by 5 minutes.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all current profile parameters unchanged.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current prebolus and bolus split strategies, using 15-20 minute preboluses for standard meals alongside active SMB/UAM, while extending weekend brunch prebolus timing slightly to blunt 120-minute peak excursions.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Telemetry shows 99.7% TIR and zero hypoglycemia. Weekend brunches display transient 180-188 mg/dL peaks that resolve completely by hour 4, indicating that minor prebolus lead-time adjustment is sufficient.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe 120-minute postprandial glucose during the next weekend brunch after extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes.

implementation_steps: Review current profile setup and confirm that all basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and target parameters are retained as configured.
For the next weekend brunch, increase prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes prior to eating, while keeping meal bolus split and e-carb settings unchanged.
Monitor glucose response at 60, 120, and 240 minutes post-brunch to confirm reduction in peak excursion without early low glucose trends.
Optionally verify in AAPS preferences that SMB activation and sensitivity toggles match intended setup.
education: Time in Range (TIR) above 90% with low glycemic variability (CV < 36%) indicates excellent insulin parameter alignment.
Postprandial peaks that return to baseline by 4 hours reflect accurate total insulin dosing (CR), where timing adjustments (prebolus) are used to address the height of the spike.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS oref1 simulate extended absorption profiles without constraining automated micro-bolusing or basal adjustments.
